newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Marks&Spencer sales rise, but shares fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Marks&Spencer sales rise, but shares fall.

text.p: Britain's biggest retailer Marks and Spencer Plc said on Wednesday Christmas came later than usual last year, but sales were up across the board and very strong in home furnishing.
Sales in the 17 weeks to January 25 rose by 8.1 percent, with clothing up 9.4 percent, homeware up 33.8 percent and food up 4.6 percent.
Sales in the five weeks to January 4 were up 6.8 percent overall, with clothing up 7.2 percent, homeware 27.7 percent and foods 4.9 percent.
"Better conditions in the housing market continued to support buoyant sales increases across the entire range of home furnishings," the retailer said in a statement.
The company's shares, which were stronger on Tuesday ahead of today's statement, were weaker on Wednesday and fell further after the figures were published.
They stood 14 pence lower at 479 pence at 1330 GMT.

"The share price moved up yesterday with people expecting a very good statement," said Nick Bubb retail analyst at MeesPierson. "It was quite a good statement but it disappointed the expectations of some people and the price has come back to a more realistic level," he said.

Marks said Christmas came late for clothing sales, but it increased its market share. Women's outerwear and men's tailoring, particularly higher-priced, more fashionable ranges, performed exceptionally well.

Better conditions in the housing market produced big sales increases in home furnishings and kitchenwear. In foods there was significant price deflation in major areas such as fruit and vegetables and peak Christmas sales came later than in previous years.
"The food sales pattern in this period reflected the lowest levels of inflation this year (1.7 percent)," Marks said.
The retailer maintained margins over the 17-week period and traded at full price until after Christmas.

"Over the period, costs have continued to increase at a similar level to sales, particularly where we provide specialised service," Marks said. The firm said higher sales volumes justified its decision earlier in the year to invest in Overseas, Marks total sales rose by 13.7 percent in the 17 weeks, measured in local currencies. Sales in Europe, excluding Britain, rose by 24.4 percent and in the Far East by 18.1 percent. Sales at Brooks Brothers in the United States rose by 9.6 percent and Kings supermarkets were up 1.5 percent.
Marks first half profits, reported in November, totalled 430.1 million pounds ($693.8 million) on sales ofo 3.53 billion. ($1=.6199 Pound)
